rows.statement: NCAA Division I infractions have a four-year statute of limitations: allegations may cover only violations from four years before the notice of inquiry, except violations affecting a current student-athlete's eligibility, a pattern of willful violations continuing into the window, blatant disregard of fundamental recruiting, extra-benefit, academic or ethical-conduct rules, or concealment.

sources.citation: NCAA, Division I Proposal 2019-3, Bylaw 19.5.11 Statute of Limitations, Adopted Final (https://web3.ncaa.org/lsdbi/search/proposalView?id=103444)
sources.quote: not earlier than four years before the date the notice of inquiry is provided to the institution

sources.citation: NCAA, Division I Proposal 2012-16, Enforcement -- New Enforcement Program, Bylaw 32.6.3 Statute of Limitations, Adopted Final (https://web3.ncaa.org/lsdbi/search/proposalView?id=3039)
sources.quote: not earlier than four years before the date the notice of inquiry is provided to the institution

sources.citation: NCAA, Enforcement process: charging (FAQ) (https://www.ncaa.org/enforcement/enforcement-process-charging)
sources.quote: generally are based on violations that have occurred four or fewer years before the time an institution is notified of an investigation

rows.notes: Three NCAA texts agree (two adopted bylaw texts, 2012 and 2019, and the current charging FAQ), so one independence group: Rulebook only. The current Division I Manual was not read (its hosts are blocked here); the 2019 proposal also changed the blatant-disregard follow-up period from one year to 18 months, not confirmed in adopted wording. Bible T9.5.1 rule 4 recalled college detect_window_years = 4 (0 of 3); this row supports it. Used by the compliance log retirement only through compliance.detect_window_years once a college rule set holds it.
